elements.scope_reason: Red-box trigger: health worker with a sharps injury OR a splash to eye/mouth/nose/broken skin, with exposure to one of the listed fluids. Three parts: (a) sharps injury, (b) splash to eye/mouth/nose/broken skin, (c) the 'with exposure to any of' conjunction.
parts_missing: Splash route (eye / mouth / nose / broken skin) is not encoded; it is replaced by the generic event 'Exposure to blood and/or body fluid', which covers any route. SNOMED has 'Exposure to biological agent via mucous membrane' (event) and 'Broken skin' (disorder), which would carry the page's routes.
'Health worker' (the exposed person is the clinician, not a patient) is not representable in the language; this is a limitation, not a builder error.

elements.scope_reason: Footnote defining the TB-symptom criterion used by the 'possible TB' conclusion: four parts, cough; fever >= 2 weeks; unexplained weight loss; drenching night sweats.
elements.problem: All four parts are present with the right concepts and 'or' logic. '>= 2 weeks' is attached to fever only, as (>= (onset Fever) (time_ago 2 weeks)) = fever began at least 2 weeks ago, which is the right direction. The footnote's punctuation ('cough, fever >= 2 weeks') can also be read as the duration applying to both cough and fever, as in the usual SA TB symptom screen (cough >= 2 weeks); the builder took the literal reading. 'Drenching' has no SNOMED qualifier; plain 'Night sweats' is the closest concept. Cough and Fever are common symptoms; Unexplained weight loss and Night sweats are not checked for on this page, which is allowed for a possible rule.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for occupational sharps/splash exposure to body fluids; Urgent: occupational sharps/splash exposure to body fluids
rule_level_problems.problem: The 'splash' half of the trigger is a clinical_finding wrapping an event-category concept ('Exposure to blood and/or body fluid', event). The briefing and gold standard express exposures as (finding (snomed_concept "Exposure to (contextual qualifier)" ...) <substance>) and never put an event concept under clinical_finding. The grammar parses it, but whether a nurse can record it in the app, and so whether the task and the priority rule ever fire on a splash without a sharps injury, is unverified. If it cannot be recorded, the whole splash branch is dead.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: occupational sharps/splash exposure to body fluids
rule_level_problems.problem: The exposure route the page names (eye / mouth / nose / broken skin) is lost: any exposure to blood/body fluid counts, including one to intact skin, which the page does not escalate. SNOMED offers 'Exposure to biological agent via mucous membrane' (event) and 'Broken skin' (disorder) if a route-specific trigger is wanted. Also, the generic event trigger overlaps the specific fluid findings: a record of 'Exposure to Blood' alone (without the generic event or a sharps injury) does not fire the rule, which may surprise a nurse who records only the specific exposure.

rule_level_problems.problem: 'Blood-stained tissue' is not in the check_for list or the priority rule; only the fluid half of that red-box item is covered (as Serosanguinous fluid). 'Human tissue' (substance) exists.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose possible TB from TB symptoms (occupational infection control)
rule_level_problems.problem: The >= 2 weeks duration is applied to fever only. The footnote 'cough, fever >= 2 weeks, ...' is ambiguous and the standard SA TB screen applies >= 2 weeks to cough; if that reading is intended, the rule fires on any cough, which is broader than the page. Question for a clinician; not a clear error.

The page addresses the health worker, not a patient. The language has no way to say that the exposed person is the clinician, so the rules will fire for any patient with a recorded sharps injury or body-fluid exposure. Not representable; worth a note in the remaining questions rather than a fix.

summary: The red box is encoded almost completely: all thirteen fluids are present with verified SNOMED substances, the priority level Urgent is justified, and the (and <trigger> (or <fluids>)) structure is right. The most consequential doubt is the splash trigger, written as a clinical_finding around an event-category concept, a form the house standard never uses; if the app cannot record it, the splash branch never fires and only sharps injuries reach Urgent. Lesser gaps: the exposure route (eye/mouth/nose/broken skin) is not captured, blood-stained tissue is missing, and the possible-TB rule's >= 2 weeks applies to fever only under one reading of an ambiguous footnote.
